reports.title: KANZHUN LIMITED Announces Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company currently expects its total revenues to be between RMB2.19 billion and RMB2.23 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 5.3% to 7.3%. This forecast reflects the Company’s current views on the market and operational conditions in China, which are subject to change and cannot be predicted with reasonable accuracy as of the date hereof.

desk.headline: Revenue up 11.7% to RMB2.42bn, just below estimates; adjusted EPS up 14%; Q4 outlook points to slower 5–7% growth

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted, diluted per ADS (RMB); prior year recast

results: Revenue rose 11.7% to RMB2.42bn, slightly short of the RMB2.44bn estimate; nearly all of it came from recruitment services to employers.
Operating income rose 23% to RMB845m and the adjusted operating margin widened to 44.5%, even as sales and marketing spend jumped 49% on advertising.
A RMB1.44bn fair-value loss on a stake in a company that listed in January pushed the quarter to a GAAP net loss of RMB249m; adjusted net income rose 12% to RMB1.07bn.
Monthly users rose 14% to 73.0m, with blue-collar workers, small firms and lower-tier cities driving growth.
Operating cash flow was RMB1.26bn (+7.6%); cash and short-term investments were RMB19.6bn. A new $500m, 12-month buyback was approved on top of the existing $400m programme.

guidance.summary: Kanzhun expects Q4 revenue of RMB2.19–2.23bn, up 5.3–7.3% from a year ago, a clear slowdown from Q3's 11.7%. It gives no profit guidance.

points: Management said growth is increasingly coming from blue-collar hiring and smaller cities, which both gained revenue share.
Price changes in tier-1 cities are largely done: free and ultra-cheap job posts have been phased out.
AI tools such as a headhunting assistant were credited with better match rates; management said it will focus on AI applications rather than racing to buy computing power.
The softer Q4 outlook reflects seasonally weak hiring and more job seekers than openings, with demand weak in autos, finance and retail but strong in manufacturing.
Returns to shareholders this year, buybacks plus dividend, have topped $530m, more than all of last year's adjusted net income.

watch: Whether Q4 revenue lands in the RMB2.19–2.23bn range as hiring slows seasonally.
Whether the margin can hold near 44% while marketing spend keeps rising.
Further swings in the value of the listed investee stake, which can move GAAP profit sharply.
